name: SBA 'grants' to start or grow a business
why: SBA says it does not give grants to start or expand a business; its grants go to nonprofits, resource partners, SBIR/STTR, and state STEP programs. Offers of an 'SBA grant' for your business are a red flag.

name: Unsolicited 'government grant' offers that ask for a fee
why: FTC warns that scammers trick small businesses into paying to apply for fake government grants.

name: 'HHS (or other agency) free grant money' messages
why: FTC alert: impostors posing as HHS or hacked friends promise grant money, then collect payments and personal data. Do not pay to get a grant.

name: Paid grant-writing services that guarantee funding
why: FTC and Florida sued 'Grant Bae' for taking thousands from minority-owned businesses with false guarantees of relief grants.

name: COVID-19 EIDL and EIDL Advance
why: EIDL loans must be repaid and are not forgivable; new applications closed Jan 1, 2022, so any current 'EIDL grant' offer is not real.

name: SBA Microloans
why: Loans up to $50,000 at roughly 8% to 13% with up to 6 years to repay, through nonprofit intermediaries; often listed alongside grants.

name: Kiva US
why: 0% interest crowdfunded loans of $1,000 to $15,000 that must be repaid over 12 to 36 months; not a grant.

name: NC Rural Center small business financing (SSBCI programs, CornerSquare)
why: The Rural Center's business funding is lending and loan support through banks and CDFIs; the page lists no grant programs.

name: NCBiotech company funding
why: NCBiotech's company money is mainly business loans ($250K to $650K, quarterly deadlines); its grants mostly go to universities and nonprofits.

name: City of Winston-Salem Small Business Loan Program
why: Loans of $5,000 to $100,000 at prime plus 1% in the NRSA; the city states grant funds are not available, though part may be forgiven (possibly taxable).

name: EDA Revolving Loan Funds
why: EDA grants capitalize local revolving loan funds; what reaches the business is a loan, not a grant.

name: NC HUB certification
why: Was a procurement certification, never funding, and the state ended HUB programs on July 7, 2026; replaced by the NC Small Business Enterprise (NCSBE) certification.
